note: Registry of named things: who makes what, and which technique each one demonstrates. Pages reference an id here and never type a name, so a rename or a retirement is one edit. An entry with no 'source' is a seed: it was listed from general knowledge or a secondary search result and has not been checked. A seed cannot be cited on a measured page until it has a primary source, a 'checked' date and 'verified': true. The build flags verified entries unchecked for 90 days. Where a technique has more than one maker, a page names at least two. The site ranks nothing and links no affiliate. This is a technique registry and not a product comparison: it carries no price, no seat cost, no setup effort and no measure of quality, and it does not list the ordinary business software an office already runs that has since grown an AI feature. The 'What the registry is, and is not' section of /method/ says what a reader who wants to buy rather than build should check for themselves. 'as_of' is the date the site prints as 'names listed', so it must never be older than the newest entry's 'checked' date; scripts/validate.py enforces that.

kinds.model: A trained model, addressed by a versioned name. 'developer' is the id of the organization that trained it.
kinds.product: Something a person uses: a chat app, a coding agent, an automation service.
kinds.tool: Something a developer builds with: a framework, a runtime, a database, a protocol, an API.
